title: Kernel-aware residency hysteresis and cohort prefetch pipeline for paged-attention
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Context: Production workloads show intermittent p95 decode latency spikes when paged attention causes hot KV pages to be recycled aggressively during bursty prefill loads. Existing simple LRU and immediate-evict heuristics cause oscillation between hotsets which hurts tail latency and increases GPU kernel churn.

Goal: Implement a kernel-aware residency hysteresis layer plus a cohort prefetch pipeline that groups related page candidates and schedules background compaction/soft-evict in a way that minimizes kernel switching and prefill stalls. The system should reduce p95 decode latency for mixed short/long sequences and lower per-token GPU time by improving reuse of decoder KV across nearby requests.

Approach summary:
- Kernel cost index (KCI): compute a lightweight per-page KCI that estimates the expected incremental kernel invocation cost if a page is migrated or loaded (uses historical prefill counts, sequence-length distribution, and last-decode delta). KCI is updated by a streaming estimator.
- Residency hysteresis: pages gain a "residency credit" when repeatedly accessed; eviction requires draining credits rather than single-touch eviction. Credits decay with an adaptive half-life tied to observed workload churn. This prevents flip-flop eviction for pages in narrow hotsets.
- Cohort prefetch pipeline: instead of prefetching individual pages on demand, we form cohorts (temporal groups of pages referenced within the same decode window) and schedule cohort prefetches with a single kernel-choice decision. Cohorts are prioritized by aggregated KCI to optimize kernel selection and minimize switching.
- Demotion queue + soft-evict window: pages targeted for eviction first enter a demotion queue where low-priority members are asynchronously written to a background compactor if reclaim is necessary. Demoted pages remain addressable for a short soft-evict window to catch near-term reuse without paying a full reload.
- Kernel-aware scheduling glue: runtime selects kernel variants for decode/prefill based on active cohort fingerprints and KCI; when a cohort aligns with a preferred kernel the runtime reduces prefetch parallelism and increases batching to amortize kernel startup.

Trade-offs considered:
- Memory overhead: residency credits and cohort bookkeeping add small metadata per page (~40 bytes). We prioritized this over more invasive per-tenant structures to keep on-device footprint bounded.
- Complexity vs wins: cohort formation requires additional commit/rollback control in the prefill path; chosen to be conservative and opt-in via a runtime flag to limit blast radius.
- Staleness vs reactivity: hysteresis improves tail but can delay reclaim of genuinely cold pages. Adaptive decay parameters mitigate long-term waste.

Design docs and artifacts:
- Design doc: Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleDriveLink (prefill cohort design, diagrams, KCI math)
- Simulation harness: GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-sim/tree/feature/cohort-prefetch (workload replay tests)
- Perf dashboard prototype: internal Grafana panel linked in PR description (compare baseline vs cohort-enabled).

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- p95 decode latency reduced by >= 15% on mixed short/long synthetic replay (95th percentile across 1M requests).
- Kernel-switch count reduced by >= 25% (measured as distinct kernel load events per 10K decodes).
- No regression (>1%) in median latency or throughput on stable long-sequence workloads.
- Memory overhead for metadata < 1% of total KV cache size in production configs.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind runtime flag and perf-tests enabled in staging.
2) Canary with 5% of traffic on paid-hosted region; monitor p95, kernel-switch, and OOMs for 48 hours.
3) Increase to 25% if stable, then to 100% with 7-day burn.

Observability and debug hooks:
- Expose per-cohort metrics: cohort_size, cohort_kci_avg, cohort_kernel_hint, cohort_prefetch_latency.
- Eviction pipeline traces: demotion_enqueue_time, soft_evict_hits, compact_success_rate.
- Debug endpoints to snapshot residency credits and recent cohort membership for a tenant.

Compatibility and migration:
- Default off. For Dedicated customers we will enable via admin config after validation. Private deployments require a minor agent bump to expose the new flags.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for credit decay and KCI estimator edge cases.
- Integration tests in simulated multi-tenant replay harness with controlled churn.
- Staging A/B with real traffic for 7 days before GA.
acceptance_criteria: p95 decode latency improvement >= 15% on mixed replay
kernel-switch events reduced by >= 25% per 10k decodes
median latency and throughput regressions <= 1% on long-sequence workloads
metadata memory overhead < 1% of KV cache size
implementation_steps: Add lightweight KCI estimator to page metadata and ensure streaming updates during prefill/decodes
Implement residency credit ledger with adaptive decay and demotion queue insertion
Build cohort assembler in prefill path and a cohort-level prefetch scheduler
Wire kernel-hint signals into runtime kernel selection API
Create background compactor and soft-evict logic with safe rollback on reuse
Add metrics, traces, and debug endpoints
Run perf harness and iterate parameters based on results
Prepare canary rollout and run staged monitoring
risks: Incorrect KCI tuning can bias prefetch toward low-value pages causing extra memory churn
Cohort assembly could add latency to single-request prefill if mis-implemented
Background compaction could contend for GPU cycles with low-priority decodes unless throttled
Metadata bugs could cause leaks across tenant boundaries if not properly scoped
